title: new(expr)
short_description: The built-in new now takes a value, not just a type, so the temporary variable goes away.
summary: Go has never let you take the address of a value that is not already in a variable. `&Config{}` works because a composite literal is addressable, but `&f()`, `&42` and `&someParam` are not, so we invented the two line dance: assign to a temporary, then take its address. Go 1.26 lets `new` accept an expression, and the dance is over.
diagram_caption: new(T) allocates a zero value of T. new(expr) allocates a new variable already holding the value of expr, and returns its address.
